tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Diagnose and review...', 'Use this skill when...') and lists numerous concrete trigger contexts phrased as user-facing symptoms (answers got worse, responses cut off, judge scores swing, fine-tuned model shipping unevaluated, etc.) rather than internal implementation details. It is pushy in enumerating many scenarios including ones where the user doesn't name the domain directly. It is a long paragraph but stays within the bounds of a 'short paragraph' as specified, and is justified by the breadth of triggering scenarios the skill must cover.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when answers got worse or a model may hallucinate more, responses are cut off or end on max_tokens, the same prompt gives different answers, a Bedrock CreateEvaluationJob or a Bedrock RAG evaluation job for a knowledge base fails or needs interpreting..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: While the vast majority of the content is domain-specific, several sections are extremely verbose and repeat the same point multiple times (e.g., the upgraded-negative table, the negative-claims section, Guardrail 9/10 all restate the same 'don't say zero errors' rule in several forms). This repetition inflates the body well beyond what's needed to convey the non-obvious rules.
tests.evidence: 'Negative claims are source-bound.' section repeats concepts already covered in Guardrail 9 and the 'Before You Present' checklist almost verbatim.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (check catalog, severities per check-id, API quirks, metric queries) is mostly pushed to references/ files and linked conditionally; the body keeps only a severity definition table and a short list of standing guardrails necessary for correct behavior, not raw lookup tables.
tests.evidence: 'Severities are the catalog's, never improvised: LLM-EVAL-001 CRITICAL, -002 HIGH, ...' is a borderline inline table but is short and essential for the delegation payload use case, not a large reference dump; full catalog lives in checks-evaluation.md.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via a markdown link in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by an explicit condition for when to load it.
tests.evidence: '[checks-evaluation.md](references/checks-evaluation.md) (load it before assigning any check-id or severity)'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/.
tests.evidence: '[metrics-and-logs.md](references/metrics-and-logs.md)' and similar — all relative, no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only guardrails, severity assignment, delegation payload, finish-reason measurement) are given exact, prescriptive rules, while flexible parts (synthesis, review prioritization) leave room for judgment, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: 'Read-only. Never call a mutating API — in particular CreateEvaluationJob...' is appropriately strict, while 'For an incident, lead with the root cause ... with the highest-impact action' leaves room for agent judgment.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple paths/tools exist (Bedrock vs SageMaker vs RAG), the skill gives a clear decision process (service check) rather than presenting them as an undifferentiated menu.
tests.evidence: 'Service check. When a job is named, confirm which service ran it: sagemaker:DescribeTrainingJob for a recipe-driven job, bedrock:GetEvaluationJob for a Bedrock-native one' gives a clear decision rule rather than an open menu.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable investigation procedure (Steps 1-5, routing table, catalog-driven checks) applicable to any Bedrock/SageMaker evaluation question, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: 'Work the steps in order... Step 1: Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support' generalizes across any evaluation investigation.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive dedicated gotchas section covering non-obvious domain pitfalls.
tests.evidence: '## Common wrong answers' section lists specific pitfalls like '"ListEvaluationJobs" is empty, so no evaluation has ever run — CRITICAL.' with corrections.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured findings/reports and provides templates in assets/ for this purpose.
tests.evidence: 'load [evaluation-report-template.md](assets/evaluation-report-template.md) for the Bedrock path and the posture review, and [sagemaker-evaluation-report-template.md](assets/sagemaker-evaluation-report-template.md)'

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The only inline template-like content is the short Findings block format, well under 20 lines; longer report templates are stored in assets/.
tests.evidence: 'Findings\n<check-id> (<SEVERITY>) — <measured <value> | no-datapoints | not-queried> — <window> — <source API> — owner:<area> — <doc URL>' is a short inline template.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three files in assets/ are linked in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each asset link specifies the trigger condition for loading it.
tests.evidence: '[delegation-payload.json](assets/delegation-payload.json) is that prompt, finished (load when delegating evidence-gathering)'

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: All asset links use relative paths rooted at assets/.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow is presented as a checkbox checklist with Step N format, and the detailed sections below reference the same step numbers.
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support' followed by '### Step 1 — Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support'.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an extensive self-validation section instructing the agent to check its own output before presenting.
tests.evidence: '## Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' with items like 'Scan the draft for an upgraded negative, sentence by sentence.'
